children.name: Bocagia
children.description: Bocagia - a genus in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Bocagia minuta
children.description: The marsh tchagra or blackcap bush-shrike (Bocagia minuta) is a species of passerine bird placed in the monotypic genus Bocagia in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Chlorophoneus
children.description: The green-and-yellow bushshrikes — a genus of medium-sized, colourful bushshrikes with greenish upperparts and bright yellow or orange underparts. They are more arboreal and slender-billed than Malaconotus, feeding primarily on insects gleaned from foliage. Their songs are rich, melodious, and often repetitive.

children.name: Chlorophoneus abscessus
children.description: A bushshrike from Central Africa.

children.name: Chlorophoneus bocagei
children.description: Bocage's bushshrike (Chlorophoneus bocagei), also known as the grey-green bushshrike, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is scatteredly present throughout central Africa. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Chlorophoneus kupeensis
children.description: The Mount Kupe bushshrike (Chlorophoneus kupeensis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It was previously thought to be endemic to Cameroon, where it is found in the Bakossi Forest Reserve and in particular on Mount Kupe, where it has been known to attract ecotourists. In 2011 it was reported to be present in two sites in south east Nigeria.

children.name: Chlorophoneus multicolor
children.description:
The many-colored bushshrike or many-coloured bushshrike (Chlorophoneus multicolor) is a species of bird in the bushshrike family, Malaconotidae.
The black-fronted bushshrike (C. Nigrifrons) of southern and eastern Africa is sometimes included in this species.

children.name: Chlorophoneus nigrifrons
children.description: The black-fronted bushshrike (Chlorophoneus nigrifrons) is a passerine bird of the bushshrike family, Malaconotidae. It inhabits forests mainly in East Africa. It forms a superspecies with the many-colored bushshrike (C. Multicolor) and the two are sometimes considered to be a single species.

children.name: Chlorophoneus olivaceus
children.description: The olive bushshrike (Chlorophoneus olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Chlorophoneus sulfureopectus
children.description: The orange-breasted bushshrike or sulphur-breasted bushshrike (Chlorophoneus sulfureopectus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. Another bird, Braun's bushshrike, is also sometimes called the orange-breasted bushshrike.

children.name: Dryoscopus
children.description: The puffbacks — a genus of medium-sized bushshrikes named for the male's dramatic display in which the loose feathers of the lower back and rump are fluffed out into a striking white ball. They are active, restless foragers with strong, slightly hooked bills, found across sub-Saharan Africa in woodlands and savannas. They are vocal birds with harsh, repetitive calls.

children.name: Dryoscopus angolensis
children.description:
The pink-footed puffback (Dryoscopus angolensis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.
It is found in western Central Africa as well as in the Albertine Rift montane forests and northern adjacent areas of Kenya, Uganda and the eastern Congo Basin. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Dryoscopus cubla
children.description: The black-backed puffback (Dryoscopus cubla) is a species of passerine bird in the family Malaconotidae. They are common to fairly common sedentary bushshrikes in various wooded habitats in Africa south of the equator. They restlessly move about singly, in pairs or family groups, and generally frequent tree canopies. Like others of its genus, the males puff out the loose rump and lower back feathers in display, to assume a remarkable ball-like appearance. They draw attention to themselves by their varied repertoire of whistling, clicking and rasping sounds. Their specific name cubla, originated with Francois Levaillant, who derived it from a native southern African name, where the "c" is an onomatopoeic click sound. None of the other five puffback species occur in southern Africa.

children.name: Dryoscopus gambensis
children.description: The northern puffback (Dryoscopus gambensis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Dryoscopus pringlii
children.description: Pringle's puffback (Dryoscopus pringlii) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in southern Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and northern Tanzania. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.

children.name: Dryoscopus sabini
children.description:
Sabine's puffback (SAY; Dryoscopus sabini), also known as the large-billed puffback, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is native to the African tropical rainforest (western and sparsely throughout Central Africa). Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical swamps.
Its common name and Latin binomial commemorate General Sir Edward Sabine.

children.name: Dryoscopus senegalensis
children.description: The red-eyed puffback (Dryoscopus senegalensis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Nigeria and Central Africa. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Dryoscopus senex
children.description: Dryoscopus senex (Pale-billed Puffback) is a bushshrikes species found in Africa region.

children.name: Laniarius
children.description: The boubous and gonoleks — a genus of colourful bushshrikes with strong, stout bills and a characteristic duetting behaviour in which pairs sing precisely coordinated antiphonals. They are among the most brightly coloured bushshrikes, often combining black, white, and brilliant crimson or yellow underparts. They are secretive but highly vocal, inhabiting dense thickets and riparian vegetation.

children.name: Laniarius aethiopicus
children.description: The Ethiopian boubou (Laniarius aethiopicus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius amboimensis
children.description: The Gabela bushshrike (Laniarius amboimensis) or Amboim bushshrike is a bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius amboinensis
children.description: A boubou from the highlands of East Africa.

children.name: Laniarius atrococcineus
children.description: The crimson-breasted shrike (Laniarius atrococcineus) or the crimson-breasted gonolek, ('gonolek' - supposedly imitative of its call), or the crimson-breasted boubou, is a southern African bird. It has black upper parts with a white flash on the wing, and bright scarlet underparts. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated it as a "least-concern species".

children.name: Laniarius atroflavus
children.description: The yellow-breasted boubou (Laniarius atroflavus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius barbarus
children.description: The yellow-crowned gonolek (Laniarius barbarus), also known as the common gonolek, is a medium-sized passerine bird in the bushshrike family..

children.name: Laniarius barbatus
children.description: A boubou with yellow breast from Central Africa.

children.name: Laniarius brauni
children.description: Braun's bushshrike (Laniarius brauni) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius erlangeri
children.description: The black boubou (Laniarius nigerrimus), also known as Somali boubou, Erlanger's boubou or coastal boubou, is a medium-size bushshrike.

children.name: Laniarius erythrogaster
children.description: The black-headed gonolek (Laniarius erythrogaster) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius fuelleborni
children.description: Fülleborn's boubou (Laniarius fuelleborni) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia, where its typical habitat is humid montane forest, dense undergrowth, secondary growth, forest edges and bamboo groves. The name of this bird commemorates the German physician Friedrich Fülleborn.

children.name: Laniarius funebris
children.description:
The slate-colored boubou or slate-coloured boubou (Laniarius funebris) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, dry savanna, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland. German naturalist Gustav Hartlaub described the slate-colored boubou in 1863. Two subspecies, funebris and degener are recognised. Within the genus Laniarius its position is unclear, but it does not appear to be closely related to the black-plumaged members of the genus such as Fuelleborn's boubou, Laniarius fuelleborni, with which some authorities had previously considered it conspecific.
The adult slate-colored boubou is 20 cm (8 in) long and wholly dark slate grey. The male and female are very similar. Immature birds have a plumage more barred with tawny brown and black.

children.name: Laniarius leucogaster
children.description: A boubou with white underparts from sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Laniarius leucorhynchus
children.description: The lowland sooty boubou (Laniarius leucorhynchus), also known as the sooty boubou, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is native to the African tropical rainforest. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.

children.name: Laniarius luehderi
children.description: Lühder's bushshrike (Laniarius luehderi) is a species of bird (a shrike) in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German naturalist ornithologist W. Lühder.

children.name: Laniarius major
children.description: The tropical boubou or bell shrike (Laniarius aethiopicus) is a medium-sized passerine bird of sub-Saharan Africa..

children.name: Laniarius mufumbiri
children.description: The papyrus gonolek (Laniarius mufumbiri) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Laniarius nigerrimus
children.description: The black boubou (Laniarius nigerrimus), also known as Somali boubou, Erlanger's boubou or coastal boubou, is a medium-size bushshrike..

children.name: Laniarius poensis
children.description: The mountain sooty boubou (Laniarius poensis), western boubou or mountain boubou, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Laniarius ruficeps
children.description: The red-naped bushshrike or red-naped boubou (Laniarius ruficeps) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae, which is native to the dry lowlands of the eastern Afrotropics.

children.name: Laniarius rufispectus
children.description: Laniarius rufispectus (Rufous-breasted Boubou) is a bushshrikes species found in Africa region.

children.name: Laniarius somalicus
children.description: A boubou from the Horn of Africa.

children.name: Laniarius sublacteus
children.description: The East Coast boubou or Zanzibar boubou (Laniarius sublacteus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Laniarius turatii
children.description:
Turati's boubou (Laniarius turatii) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, and Sierra Leone. Its natural habitat is moist savanna.
The common name and Latin binomial commemorates the Milanese banker Ercole Turati (1829-1881) who also collected natural history specimens.

children.name: Laniarius willardi
children.description: Willard's sooty boubou (Laniarius willardi) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae, native to the Albertine Rift montane forests.

children.name: Malaconotus
children.description: The large bushshrikes — a genus of robust, heavy-billed African passerines with powerful hooked bills adapted for taking large prey including vertebrates. They are the largest bushshrikes, with a deliberate, slow-moving foraging style that belies their fierce predatory nature. Their calls are deep, mournful whistles that carry long distances through the forest.

children.name: Malaconotus alius
children.description: The Uluguru bushshrike (Malaconotus alius) is a species of rare bird occurring only in the Uluguru Mountains in Morogoro Region of Tanzania. It was discovered in 1926 and was known to be confined to a single site in the Uluguru North Forest Reserve of about 84 km2. However, in March 2007, a team of Wildlife Conservation Society of Tanzania discovered its presence in the Uluguru South Forest Reserve in Morogoro Region. There are an estimated 1200 pairs remaining and the population trend is stable.

children.name: Malaconotus blanchoti
children.description: The grey-headed bushshrike (Malaconotus blanchoti), colloquially known as the ghostbird, is a species of passerine bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is widespread throughout sub-Saharan Africa, although relatively absent in Central Africa and the interior of southern Africa. It is the most widespread species of its genus, which consists of large bushshrikes with massive bills and mournful hooting calls. It occurs sparsely in a range of wooded habitats, though typically in denser vegetation within dry or moist savannah. The monogamous pairs occupy woodland with sufficient cover. They are sedentary, but will undertake limited post-breeding movements.

children.name: Malaconotus cruentus
children.description: The fiery-breasted bushshrike (Malaconotus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Malaconotus gladiator
children.description:
The green-breasted bushshrike or gladiator bushshrike (Malaconotus gladiator) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in the Cameroonian Highlands forests. With a total length of and a body mass of around this may be the largest of the Malaconotidae.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Malaconotus lagdeni
children.description: Lagden's bushshrike (Malaconotus lagdeni) is a bird species in the bushshrike family (Malaconotidae) native to Africa. It is a stocky bird with yellow or orange-yellow underparts, olive green upperparts, a grey head and heavy bill. Two subspecies are recognised.

children.name: Malaconotus monteiri
children.description: Monteiro's bushshrike (Malaconotus monteiri) is a species of bird in the bush-shrike family (Malaconotidae).

children.name: Nilaus
children.description: Nilaus — a genus of bushshrikes in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Nilaus afer
children.description: The brubru (Nilaus afer) is a species of bushshrike (family Malaconotidae) found in most of Sub-Saharan Africa. It is the only member of the genus Nilaus.

children.name: Rhodophoneus
children.description: A monotypic genus of bushshrike containing the Rosy-patched Bushshrike, a striking inhabitant of arid scrublands in eastern Africa. It has a unique plumage pattern with a vivid crimson patch on the throat and breast, and is more terrestrial than other bushshrikes, often running on the ground.

children.name: Rhodophoneus cruentus
children.description: The rosy-patched bushshrike (Rhodophoneus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Rhodophoneus. It is found in Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, and Tanzania. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Tchagra
children.description: The tchagras — a genus of medium-sized bushshrikes with a distinctive crown pattern featuring a black lateral stripe edged with white, giving them a capped appearance. They have relatively slender, hooked bills and long, graduated tails, and are more terrestrial than other bushshrikes. They inhabit scrub, savanna, and forest edge habitats across Africa.

children.name: Tchagra australis
children.description: The brown-crowned tchagra (Tchagra australis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Tchagra jamesi
children.description: The three-streaked tchagra (Tchagra jamesi) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae, which is an uncommon resident of semi-desert regions in the eastern Afrotropics. The binomial of this bird commemorates the explorer Frank Linsly James, who also had the Frank James Memorial Hospital built in his honour.

children.name: Tchagra minuta
children.description: The marsh tchagra or blackcap bush-shrike (Bocagia minuta) is a species of passerine bird placed in the monotypic genus Bocagia in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Tchagra senegala
children.description:
The black-crowned tchagra (Tchagra senegalus) is a bushshrike. This family of passerine birds is closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and was once included in that group.
This species is found in the Arabian Peninsula and most of Africa in scrub, open woodland, semi-desert and cultivation.

children.name: Tchagra senegalus
children.description: The black-crowned tchagra (Tchagra senegalus) is a bushshrike..

children.name: Tchagra tchagra
children.description:
The southern tchagra (Tchagra tchagra) is a passerine bird found in dense scrub and coastal bush in southern and south-eastern South Africa and Eswatini.
This species is a bushshrike, a group closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and formerly included in that family.

children.name: Telophorus
children.description: A genus of beautiful, colourful bushshrikes with green upperparts and brightly coloured underparts in shades of orange, red, or yellow. They are forest and woodland dwellers that forage actively in the canopy, gleaning insects from leaves. Their songs are rich, musical, and often delivered in duet.

children.name: Telophorus cruentus
children.description: The rosy-patched bushshrike (Rhodophoneus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae..

children.name: Telophorus dohertyi
children.description:
Doherty's bushshrike (Telophorus dohertyi) is a colourful but skulking species of bush-shrike of the family Malaconotidae which is found in forest habitats in north-central Africa.
The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the American collector William Doherty.

children.name: Telophorus olivaceus
children.description: The olive bushshrike (Chlorophoneus olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Telophorus quadricolor
children.description: The gorgeous bushshrike (Telophorus viridis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is also known as the four-coloured bushshrike. Some use the name gorgeous bushshrike for the subspecies Telophorus viridis viridis only.

children.name: Telophorus viridis
children.description: The gorgeous bushshrike (Telophorus viridis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

children.name: Telophorus zeylonus
children.description:
The bokmakierie (Telophorus zeylonus) is a bushshrike. This family of passerine birds is closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and was once included in that group. This species is endemic to southern Africa, mainly in South Africa and Namibia, with an isolated population in the mountains of eastern Zimbabwe and western Mozambique. It is a species of open habitats, including karoo scrub, fynbos and parks and gardens in urban areas. The bulky cup nest is constructed in a hedge, scrub or tree fork. The 2–6, usually three, red-brown or lilac-blotched greenish-blue eggs are incubated by both sexes for about 16 days to hatching, with another 18 days to fledging.
The adult bokmakierie is a 22–23 cm long bird with olive-green upperparts and a conspicuous bright yellow tip to the black tail. The head is grey with a yellow supercilium, and the strong bill has a hooked upper mandible. The underparts are bright yellow with a broad black collar between the throat and breast, which continues up the neck sides through the eye to the bill. The legs and feet are blue-grey. The sexes are similar, but juveniles are a dull grey-green below, and lack the black gorget.
